the cytotoxic effect of QD, erythromycin, and levofloxacine was tested using 3T3 murine fibroblast cells and Eahy926 human endothelial cells.

quinupristins/dalfopristins (QD) is cytotoxic to murine fibroblast and human endothelial cells in vitro, and that this effect correlates with the frequency of infusion phlebitics observed with this drug in clinical practice.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and fast test system for predicting the local tolerability of antimicrobial agents.
the prediction of the local adverse effects of antimicrobial agents.
the in vitro assessment of the cytotoxicity of three antimicrobial agents with different local tolerability profiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results from these in vitro assays are in accordance with clinical observations.
QD is cytotoxic in vitro and may induce phlebitis when being administered intravascularly, whereas levofloxacin is not cytotoxic in vitro, but may still induce phlebitic reactions.
the cytotoxicity of QD is significantly higher than that of levofloxacin, and the cytotoxicity induced by erythromycin is significantly higher than levofloxacin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the in vitro cytotoxicity assay is a useful tool to assess the potential of an antibiotic to induce local adverse events when being administered parenterally.
quinupristins/dalfopristins and erythromycins show cytotoxic effects in murine and human cells in vitro, while levofloxacin does not.

the cytotoxic effects of QD on 3T 3 and Eahy 926 cells were higher than those of erythromycin or levofloxacin and that Eahy 926 endothelial cells seem to be less sensitive to cytotoxins than 3T  3 fibroblastic cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytotoxicity assays used here can serve as a tool to predict the local tolerability of parenteral antibiotics.
the in vitro assays used are able to predict the in vivo effects on the vascular endothelium.
the use of QD is associated with a higher risk of infusion phlebititis than other antibiotics.
